newsitem.title: UK: Western firms urge action on Russia PSA amendments.
newsitem.headline: Western firms urge action on Russia PSA amendments.

text.p: Western oil industry executives urged Russia on Friday to speed up amendments to production sharing agreement (PSA) laws, saying lack of clear-cut legislation was stalling foreign investment.
"Regulation needs to be put in place," Frank Duffield, President of the Moscow-based Sakhalin Energy Investment Company told a conference on the Russian oil industry in London.
Sakhalin Energy Investment represents foreign shareholders in an oil and gas project off Russia's Far East Sakhalin island known as Sakhalin II.
"We have adopted a phased development approach to see how legislation progresses but it is becoming increasingly difficult to reassure my investors," Duffield said.
Sakhalin Energy Investment's shareholders are USX Marathon with 30 percent, Mitsui with 20 percent, McDermott with 20 percent, Royal Dutch/Shell with 20 percent amd Mitsubishi with 10 percent.

Duffield welcomed news the Russian State Duma, the lower house of parliament, was to hold the first reading of a draft law to approve a list of oil and gas blocks eligible for production sharing on March 20.
Approval of the draft law would pave the way for further PSA amendments.
"It is crucial that it's successful," said Duffield
Alexei Mikhailov, chairman of the State Duma's Natural Resources Committee told the conference he was optimistic the draft would go through.
"It's an important sign that the Duma has actually set aside a whole afternoon to discuss the draft on March 20," he said.
He added that until the law on the list was approved it was unlikely further ammendments on the PSAs could be carried out.

"Until the question of the list is settled it's unlikely the Duma will discuss other PSA issues," he said. "Parliament wants to know how many blocks will be involved. Is it a handful, a dozen or hundreds?"
Mikhailov said he expected roughly 20 blocks to be included on the list against an original list including some 250 fields.
The Paris-based International Energy Agency also stressed the need for amendments in the PSAs.
"As long as the major concerns in the legal framework for PSAs remain unresolved, pending projects are unlikely to advance," the IEA said in a paper prepared for the conference.
"Investors consider passage of the Law of Amendments and Law on Lists essential for PSAs to become effective," the paper said.
